paper.title: Fast Rates for Bandit PAC Multiclass Classification

settings.name_in_paper: Agnostic PAC bandit multiclass classification (finite hypothesis class)
unmapped: Multiclass classification structure: each example has a single correct label; reward of a label is the indicator that it equals the true label (sparse 0/1 rewards)
Agnostic PAC objective relative to a finite hypothesis class H of size N (N_exp = |H|); output hypothesis must be eps-optimal in 0-1 loss
Computational access through a weighted ERM oracle over H
settings.definition_quote: In the PAC version of the problem, given parameters $\eps, \delta > 0$ the goal of the learner is to produce a hypothesis $\hat{h} : \calX \to \calY$, such that with probability at least $1 - \delta$ ... $L_\calD(\hat{h}) - L_\calD(h^\star) \leq \eps$

unmapped: Multiclass classification structure with single correct label (sparse 0/1 rewards)
Possibly infinite hypothesis class with finite Natarajan dimension d_N
settings.definition_quote: Let $\calH : \calX \to \calY$ be a hypothesis class of finite Natarajan dimension $d_N$.

unmapped: Smoothness and Lipschitzness with respect to the L1 norm (gradients bounded in L_inf)

algorithms.name: Bandit PAC Multiclass Classification via Log Barrier Stochastic Optimization (Algorithm 1)
Stochastic Frank-Wolfe with SPIDER gradient estimates

symbols.N_exp: size of the finite hypothesis class |H| (paper's N)

tuning: SPIDER FW run for T = Theta((K^4/gamma^4) sqrt(log(N/delta))) rounds, eta_t = 1/t, batch sizes b_t = (gamma/2K)^2 t^2 at t=2^k-1, b_t = t otherwise

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: If we set $\gamma = \frac12$, $M_1 = \Theta(K^8 \log \brk{N / \delta})$, $M_2 = \Theta \brk*{\log \brk{N / \delta} \brk*{K / \eps + 1 / \eps^2}}$ ... then with probability at least $1-\delta$ \cref{alg:bandit-pac} outputs $\hat{h} \in \calH$ with $L_\calD(\hat{h}) - L_\calD(h^\star) \leq \eps$, using a total sample complexity of $O ((K^9 + \frac{1}{\eps^2}) \log\frac{N}{\delta} )$. Furthermore, ... makes a total number of $O(K^4 \sqrt{\log(N / \delta)})$ calls to the weighted ERM oracle ... runs in total time polynomial in $K$, $1 / \eps$ and $\log(N / \delta)$.

results.notes: Proper learner; polynomial time given a weighted ERM oracle with O(1) cost per call; O(K^4 sqrt(log(N/delta))) oracle calls.

symbols.d_N: Natarajan dimension of the hypothesis class

conditions: hypothesis class has finite Natarajan dimension d_N

source.label: thm:natarajan-main
source.quote: Let $\calH : \calX \to \calY$ be a hypothesis class of finite Natarajan dimension $d_N$. Then there exists a bandit multiclass classification algorithm which outputs a hypothesis $\hat h$ with $L_\calD(\hat h) - \inf_{h \in \calH} L_\calD(h) \leq \eps$ with a sample complexity of $\widetilde{O} ((K^9 + 1/\eps^2)d_N \log(1/\delta))$.

results.notes: Probability 1-delta implicit (PAC model). Obtained via Proposition 1 (discretization with s samples then Theorem 1 on finite cover). Stated as existence; computational efficiency not discussed.

symbols.D_1: L1 diameter of the domain W
symbols.t_it: iteration number of the Frank-Wolfe algorithm

conditions: f convex, beta-smooth and G-Lipschitz w.r.t. L1 norm
tuning: b_t = (G/(beta D))^2 t^2 if t in {2^k-1}, b_t = t otherwise

source.label: thm:fw-generic
source.quote: \cref{alg:fw} with step sizes $\eta_t = 1/t$ and batch sizes $b_t$ defined as ... guarantees that, for all $t \geq 2$ and any $\delta>0$: $\E\sbr{ F(w_{t}) - F(w^*) } \leq \frac{25\beta D^2}{t} \sqrt{\log{d}}$, and $\Pr( F(w_{t}) - F(w^*) \leq \frac{25\beta D^2}{t} \sqrt{\log\frac{dt}{\delta}} ) \geq 1-\delta$.

results.notes: Out-of-scope optimization subroutine result; optimization error in expectation after t iterations (not sample count).

conditions: f convex, beta-smooth and G-Lipschitz w.r.t. L1 norm
tuning: b_t = (G/(beta D))^2 t^2 if t in {2^k-1}, b_t = t otherwise

source.label: thm:fw-generic
source.quote: $\Pr( F(w_{t}) - F(w^*) \leq \frac{25\beta D^2}{t} \sqrt{\log\frac{dt}{\delta}} ) \geq 1-\delta$. Consequently, for convergence to within $\epsilon > 0$ with probability at least $1-\delta$, the algorithm requires $O((\beta D^2/\epsilon) \sqrt{\log(d/\delta)})$ calls to LOO and $O(((G^2D^2 + \beta^2 D^4)/ \epsilon^2) \log(d/\delta))$ stochastic gradient computations.
